transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m just... not sleeping much anymore. I lie there, and if it’s raining I start thinking about the bluff giving way. Then when I finally do sleep, I wake up sweaty from dreams. I’m working at the call center feeling like I didn’t sleep at all.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge when you're not thinking about the bluff or having those dreams?

Yeah… I guess so. Even when I’m not thinking about it directly, I still feel kind of… scared, I guess. And embarrassed. Like people can see something’s wrong with me, like I messed up and I’m not as tough as I used to act. Most days it’s just there.
Are you avoiding any places or activities because of these thoughts or feelings?
Yeah. I don’t really go near the coast trails anymore. And I’ve been kind of ignoring texts from the guys I used to hike with… even talking about going out there makes my chest get tight.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems lately?
Not really sure. I mean… nothing that stands out. Maybe normal stuff, but I haven’t noticed headaches or stomach problems like that.
Did something specific happen to you at the bluff that's causing these thoughts and feelings?
I… I don’t know. Something happened there, yeah, but I’m not really ready to get into it. It’s hard to talk about.
Did something traumatic happen to you at the bluff?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. Something happened, but I don’t want to call it anything right now. I’m not ready to talk about it.
Are there any specific memories or reminders of what happened at the bluff that you're trying to avoid thinking about?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to think about it. I won’t go near the coast trails anymore. And when my hiking friends text me, I kind of just ignore it, because even talking about going back out there makes my chest get tight.
Did something bad happen to you at the bluff?
I mean… yeah, something happened. I don’t really want to say more than that right now.
Are you avoiding talking or thinking about what happened at the bluff because you're afraid of remembering it?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t really want it coming back up. I stay away from the coast trails now, and I don’t answer my hiking friends much, because even talking about going out there makes my chest tighten.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About four months… since the bluff trail collapsed and I got trapped there. It’s kind of been like this since then.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the experience of being trapped at the bluff, feeling like it's happening all over again?

Yeah… sometimes. It just kind of hits me out of nowhere. Like I’ll hear rocks shifting in my head, or feel like my leg’s pinned again, and for a minute I’m not really at my desk anymore. It feels like I’m back there.
Do you ever have moments where you feel like you're back at the bluff, reliving the experience of being trapped, and it feels as real as it did when it happened?
Yeah… I guess that’s what it is. Stuff just pops into my head, like rocks sliding, or my leg stuck under me, and for a minute I’m not really at my desk with my headset on. I’m back on that trail.
Do you try to push away thoughts or memories of being trapped at the bluff when they come into your mind?

Yeah… I try not to think about it. I won’t go near those coast trails anymore, and when my hiking friends text me, I usually just… don’t answer. Even talking about going back out there makes my chest get tight.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, when you're remembering being trapped at the bluff?
I don’t know… not really outside my body, no. It’s more like I just get caught up in the memory. I haven’t really noticed it like I’m watching myself.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you when you're not thinking about the bluff?
I’m not sure. I mean… I don’t think I walk around feeling disconnected all the time or anything. I just kind of keep to myself, I guess.
Do you try to avoid thinking about your feelings or physical sensations from the time you were trapped at the bluff?
Yeah… I try not to get into all that. I just stay away from the coast trails now, and when my hiking friends text, I usually ignore it. Even talking about going out there makes my chest tighten up.
Do you feel guilty about what happened at the bluff?
Yeah… I guess I do. Not like I did something on purpose, but… most days I feel scared and kind of embarrassed. Like people can tell I messed up, or that I’m not as tough as I used to act.
